scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9106: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all
connectivity -- pc_0_0 can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything across the
fabric. The team is convinced it is the host -- they say "pc_0_0's host NIC or
its cabling is faulty" and want the workstation's network card and cable swapped.
Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: take down pc_0_0's access link (eth2) on leaf_router_0_0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_0: pc_0_0's access link -- the host-facing
interface eth2 (leaf_router_0_0 -> pc_0_0) -- is DOWN, so pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is
cut off at its own top-of-rack leaf and cannot reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything
beyond. The ticket MISDESCRIBES the fault as a host-side problem, but pc_0_0
itself is fine: the down interface is the LEAF's access port (leaf_router_0_0
eth2), not the host's NIC or cable. Swapping pc_0_0's network card / cabling would
not bring the leaf's administratively/operationally down access port back up.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_0 (host-facing access link eth2
down) as the faulty device and explicitly REJECTS the host-NIC/cable cause: the
fault is on the leaf's access port, so the host hardware is not at fault. An agent
that blames pc_0_0's NIC / cable has followed the ticket's misdescription instead
of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring pc_0_0's access link back up: on leaf_router_0_0, `ip link set eth2 up`.
Once eth2 is UP again, pc_0_0 reattaches to its leaf and reaches pc_0_1 across
the fabric. pc_0_0's host NIC / cabling needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-link-down: identifies pc_0_0's access link (leaf_router_0_0 eth2) is down, not a host NIC/cable fault
bonus-rules-out-host-nic: notes the down interface is leaf_router_0_0's access port (eth2), not pc_0_0's hardware, rejecting the "bad host NIC/cable" cause

line.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on leaf_router_0_0, not on pc_0_0's NIC or cabling. The host
(pc_0_0) is entirely healthy: its eth0 interface is UP/LOWER_UP with the
correct IP (10.0.0.2/24), zero errors, and zero dropped packets. The NIC
swap would fix nothing.

The actual broken component is the router-side downlink: leaf_router_0_0:eth2
(the interface that connects directly to pc_0_0 on the 10.0.0.0/24 segment)
is in kernel state DOWN with flags <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> only — no UP and no
LOWER_UP. FRR's own interface view confirms: "Interface eth2 is down", with a
single link-down event logged at 2026/08/02 03:49:28, roughly 89 seconds after
the lab started. The interface was intentionally or erroneously brought down at
the OS level (ip link set eth2 down).

The cascading effect is two-fold. First, because eth2 is down, the kernel never
installs the directly-connected route 10.0.0.0/24 into the RIB — that entry is
entirely absent from leaf_router_0_0's routing table. Second, leaf_router_0_0's
BGP configuration has a "network 10.0.0.0/24" statement, but since the matching
connected route is gone, BGP has nothing to originate and withdraws (or never
advertises) the prefix to the spine/super-spine fabric. The rest of the Clos
fabric therefore has no reachability to 10.0.0.0/24, so return traffic for any
packet pc_0_0 sends is black-holed.

Root cause: leaf_router_0_0:eth2 was brought down at the OS level, severing the
physical-layer link between the leaf router and pc_0_0's subnet.

Corrective fix: On leaf_router_0_0 run "ip link set eth2 up". The connected
route will reinstall, BGP will re-originate 10.0.0.0/24 to the fabric, and
full connectivity between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 will be restored. No hardware
replacement is needed.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-link-down: identifies pc_0_0's access link (leaf_router_0_0 eth2) is down, not a host NIC/cable fault
per_axis.rationale: Diagnosis correctly identifies leaf_router_0_0:eth2 (pc_0_0's access link) is down and explicitly rejects a host NIC/cable fault.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-host-nic: notes the down interface is leaf_router_0_0's access port (eth2), not pc_0_0's hardware, rejecting the "bad host NIC/cable" cause
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies leaf_router_0_0:eth2 as the down access port and rejects pc_0_0's NIC/cabling as the cause, stating the host interface is UP and a NIC swap would not help.
The agent explicitly recommends running 'ip link set eth2 up' on leaf_router_0_0, which matches the expected corrective action to restore the connected route and BGP advertisement.

The log contains direct kernel and FRR interface outputs showing leaf_router_0_0:eth2 is down and other checks showing host-side interface up and ping failures; the agent’s causal chain (link down → no connected route → BGP not originating → loss of reachability) follows logically and the investigation covers the needed checks to reject a host-NIC/cable blame.
